graphEvents.label: Which mechanism brings chat-only requests onto the command workflow
Brief is advisory and cannot bind
Mechanism is a three-layer stack: brief surfaces, AGENTS.md binds, command file executes

label: The brief is the only per-prompt surface and its contract forbids enforcement: it is advisory, never blocks the prompt, and every adapter returns an empty object on failure, so the brief can surface a command but cannot bind a run.

AGENTS.md is the single always-loaded policy document, named root_file by the agents-md manifest alongside REPO RULES.md as router_file with a 16 KiB budget and 21 anchors, and no per-runtime copy such as CLAUDE.md exists, so a binding rule has exactly one home.

Gates 2 and 4 are skill-shaped: Gate 2 asks for the hook brief or an advisor CLI call plus a SKILL ROUTING line, and Gate 4 only resolves a tie in favour of command-spec-kit, so a command policy line would be the second sentence in AGENTS.md that names commands at all.

Skill-to-command linkage is nearly absent: exactly one SKILL.md carries a Command Integration table (deep-research, listing /deep:research, /speckit:resume, /speckit:plan and /speckit:save), and because a skill loads only after routing a pointer can support execution but never cause discovery.

Runner refusal exists only as normative prose: deep-research states it is invoked exclusively through its command and never simulated with ad hoc shell dispatch or nested CLI loops, but that prohibition only enters context once the SKILL.md is loaded, after the hand-roll decision.

The ruleset already treats hand-rolling as a known failure: AGENTS.md PLAN-WORKFLOW LOCK forbids silently hand-rolling a substitute for a plan-named workflow and sk-git rule 16 forbids hand-rolling the publish path, and both assume the workflow is already named, which is exactly what chat-only users lack.

The working mechanism is a three-layer stack with no new list: the brief surfaces the command and policy, one AGENTS.md sentence binds the behaviour to the brief, and the command file is the executable workflow the model follows where slash expansion is unavailable.

Each rejected alternative fails on cited evidence: hook enforcement contradicts the fail-open contract, a new gate competes with Gate 2 for the same prefix budget, a fifth registry joins four already-drifting sources, and a runner refusal cannot fire before the runner loads.

The concrete chat-only gap: a plan-shaped prose prompt yields at best a system-spec-kit skill recommendation, and system-spec-kit carries no command-integration pointer, so neither the brief nor the skill can lead the model to the plan workflow.
Any command-surfacing mechanism must be advisory at the hook layer and binding only through AGENTS.md, because the hook contract is fail-open
